rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods <U+2013> two-year (2005, 2006) field experiment at Talat Demiroren research station, Sanliurfa, with SSDI and surface drip at six irrigation levels, three replications. Q2: Results and conclusions, Table 3, Fig. 1 <U+2013> muskmelon yield measured under SSDI and surface drip; regression with a dummy indicator showed no significant difference between systems across both years, but surface drip yielded significantly more in 2005 and SSDI significantly more in 2006, i.e. mixed yield outcome consistent with the claim. Q7: Results/Conclusions <U+2013> authors state from their own quadratic yield functions that irrigation must be about 83% (SSDI) and 92% (surface drip) of class A pan evaporation for maximum yield, and that any reduction below these amounts reduces yield and fruit size under semi-arid conditions (water amount as a stated requirement).
rows.notes: Single site, single crop (one cultivar), single clay soil, plot scale; only one method (harvest yield measurement with ANOVA/regression). Total plant water use is reported but no soil-water or other intermediate variable is analysed as the mechanism for the SSDI vs surface drip yield difference. No limitations of the study are stated. Only letter groupings, p-values and r2 values are given; no SD/SE/CI for yields. Q7 is borderline: the water-amount condition relates to yield response under each system rather than to the SSDI-vs-surface comparison per se.

notes: Full text available including tables and figure equations; some figure text is garbled by layout but results are legible.
